transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-28 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Priya (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Jamal (VectorCloud Head Cloud Partnerships), Elena (VectorCloud CTO), Tara (VectorCloud Solutions Architect)

Summary: quick partner discovery to map integration surface for VectorCloud's managed GPU onramp, and to define pilot scope for co-sell POC.

[00:00] Priya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh I think we have like 50 minutes on the calendar so we can cover intros, a little bit of the go-to-market and then hand off to Marco for the technical bits. how's that sound?
[00:12] Jamal (VectorCloud): sounds great, thanks Priya. quick intro — I'm Jamal, I run partnerships here at VectorCloud, we do managed GPU pools for enterprise apps, and we're exploring partner onramps for inference workloads.
[00:22] Elena (VectorCloud): hi, Elena here, CTO, curious about the private deployment and latency story.
[00:28] Tara (VectorCloud): and I'm Tara, solutions architect, I'll be owning integration work.
[00:33] Priya (Redwood): awesome, quick intros on our side — Marco's our performance SE who'll dig into latency, kernels, and the runtime; I'll own the partnership flow and commercial.

[01:05] Marco (Redwood): hey, hi all — just to set expectations I'll want to see a sample workload and request length distribution, and then we can talk about batch strategies, kv cache usage, and quantization profiles.

[01:30] Jamal: thanks. high level — VectorCloud wants to offer Redwood as a first-class inference option inside our control plane. customers would want to spin up Redwood-backed endpoints in their VPCs, or have us offer a managed "redwood-on-vector" offering. so two modes basically.
[01:48] Priya: yep, that matches how partners typically come in — either we do private deployment (we ship a customer-managed control plane into their VPC) or you run Redwood Dedicated on your GPU pool with partnership billing. both are supported.
[02:10] Elena: clarification — the private deployment you mentioned is that fully air-gapped on prem, or can it be VPC-to-VPC? we have customers with strict data residency needs.
[02:20] Marco: we have a couple variants — private control plane which is customer-networked (VPC peering or PrivateLink) and an on-prem package for air-gapped. small differences in integrability — the on-prem package needs more ops work on both sides.
[02:35] Tara: ok, for our initial pilot we want VPC peering and bring-your-own-KMS. is BYOK KMS supported? any HSM requirement?
[02:46] Priya: yes BYOK is supported, we have KMS integrations and HSM optional in the Private offering. quick note — we might need to validate FIPS/HSM depends on the customer's compliance bar.

[03:12] Jamal: on the go-to-market side, we're picturing co-sell leads, revenue share for pilots, and a potential marketplace listing afterwards. what's Redwood's standard partner revenue share?
[03:25] Priya: we have a partner program — revenue share ranges depending on co-sell motion and commitment. for pilots we typically do a reduced fee or credit, then convert to a committed monthly for Dedicated. I'll share the partner deck with details.

[04:00] Marco: jumping back to tech — question for Tara, what's your typical request profile? short chatty prompts or long generative sequences?
[04:10] Tara: mostly short to medium — avg input 120 tokens, output 200, but we do some batch retrieval use-cases with longer outputs for summarization.
[04:20] Marco: perfect. do you have a trace or histogram? even a day or week of traces helps with sizing.
[04:25] Tara: yeah I can grab a one-week trace and remove pii — we'll upload to the shared bucket.

[05:00] Jamal: couple of concerns we've heard from customers: latency SLA vs cost, and fallback if you hit capacity — what does Redwood do for graceful degradation?
[05:12] Priya: Great question. Redwood supports smart routing — fallbacks to cheaper/quantized model variants, region fallback, and a burst policy if you have Dedicated capacity. We also expose metrics per token so you can see cost tradeoffs.
[05:30] Marco: technical detail — runtime does continuous batching and kv cache — for chatty use-cases kv cache reduces token cost and latency for multi-turn. that will matter for your conversational customers.
[05:45] Elena: ok, how much ops work on VectorCloud's side for Dedicated? I'm thinking about autoscaling and node replacement.
[05:55] Priya: Dedicated is turnkey from Redwood side for model serving and autoscaling policies. you configure GPU pool sizes and policies; we can expose autoscaling hooks so VectorCloud's control plane can trigger more capacity if needed.

[06:30] Tara: what about secure telemetry and logs — customers need audit logs retained for 1 year. is that supported?
[06:36] Marco: yes, audit logs can be exported to your S3 or to your SIEM and retention is configurable. for Private deployments logs can stay in your account.

[07:10] Jamal: any concerns about model licensing? are open models fine or do you recommend model hosting constraints?
[07:18] Priya: we ship a model catalog with vetted open models; licensing depends on the model provider. for enterprise customers we can host customer-private models, but we have to align on footprint and resource use.

[07:50] Elena: let's talk perf — Marco, what's the best way to benchmark with minimal friction?
[07:55] Marco: send a week of traces and we run a perf job against your target instance class. we'll produce a latency p95, throughput curves, and cost per 1M tokens. ideally provide request concurrency and any max sequence lengths.

[08:25] Tara: question about quantization — some of our workloads are sensitive to quality. how are regressions guarded?
[08:33] Marco: Redwood Optimize provides quantization profiles and an eval harness. we recommend baseline evals using your prompt sets; we run quality regressions and can tie alerts to prompt sets.

[09:05] Jamal: you mentioned a "Smart routing" earlier — is that per-tenant policy? or global?
[09:12] Priya: policies can be per-tenant or global; your control plane can select by policy — latency-first or cost-first. we can also do canary rollouts for model versioning.

[09:45] Tara: on the integration level, what's the simplest path for VectorCloud to be able to provision endpoints into customer VPCs? API calls? terraform?
[09:56] Marco: we expose APIs and a terraform provider. for partners we have a partner onboarding template to automate provisioning.

[10:30] Jamal: curious about billing integration — can we surface Redwood usage in our billing UI for customers and have a consolidated bill?
[10:40] Priya: yes we have partner billing options — consolidated billing, marketplace integrations, or partner-managed billing. details live in the partner financials doc; I'll attach.

[11:05] Elena: security — SSO/SAML, RBAC — any gaps?
[11:12] Marco: SSO/SAML is supported; RBAC at token/route level. for Private we can synchronize to your IdP. also we've got SOC 2 and ISO references in the security pack.

[11:45] Tara: do you have prebuilt connectors for common KMS vendors? we use HashiCorp and AWS KMS.
[11:52] Priya: both supported. HashiCorp, AWS, GCP KMS; HSM options for higher compliance tiers.

[12:20] Jamal: question on model variants — if a customer needs a proprietary foundation model, can we host that in the Dedicated pool?
[12:28] Marco: yes, private model hosting is possible, but we'll need model artifacts and a compatibility check for architecture and ops. some models require special kernels or quantization steps.

[12:50] Speaker 4 (ambiguous): mm-hmm

[13:15] Tara: network egress — if we provision in customer VPC, is egress charged separately? any recommendations on NAT vs egress endpoints?
[13:24] Priya: egress pricing depends on deployment mode. For private deployments traffic stays in customer account; gateway patterns are recommended. We can provide a cost breakdown in the sizing doc.

[14:00] Marco: quick note on latency — for short prompts p50 is dominated by token generation; if you can afford slightly larger instances you get better steady-state throughput. also continuous batching helps when you have many concurrent small requests.

[14:30] Jamal: do you support GPU heterogeneity — like mixing A100 and H100 in a cluster?
[14:36] Marco: we do heterogeneous pools but we recommend homogenous pools for predictable latency. we can route workloads to compatible instance classes when needed.

[15:05] Elena: what about maintenance windows and expected downtime?
[15:12] Priya: for Dedicated we have SLA-backed uptime and planned maintenance with notifications; Private depends on customer patching cadence but we provide hotfixes and ops guidance.

[15:40] Tara: any known issues with multi-tenant KV cache when using shared pools?
[15:46] Marco: KV cache is per-tenant keyed; in shared pools we isolate caches logically. performance-wise cache warmup is still needed on cold starts.

[16:20] Jamal: customers ask about fallback models if the primary model regresses after quantization — do you expose model rollback hooks?
[16:28] Marco: yes, rollbacks and canary policies are standard. Redwood's rollout system supports automatic fallback if error rates or regressions exceed thresholds.

[16:55] Priya: commercial question — what's your target timeline to launch a pilot?
[17:02] Jamal: we want a POC in Q1, ideally early Feb, 4-6 week pilot per customer.

[17:20] Priya: sounds doable. I'll coordinate partner credits and pilot terms with our partner ops.

[18:00] Tara: on security docs — can you share SOC 2 and network diagrams? we'll need them for our sales engineers.
[18:06] Priya: yes, will share security pack and a blank network diagram.

[18:40] Marco: action item for us — once you share traces, we'll run a perf estimate and then propose instance classes for Dedicated vs Hosted pricing.

[19:05] Jamal: any blockers on legal/contracting? we usually want a co-sell addendum and reseller terms.
[19:12] Priya: we'll loop in legal. do you have an NDA?
[19:16] Jamal: yes, I'll send it after the call.

[19:40] Elena: quick question — are there any model governance tools — e.g., token filtering, PII redaction?
[19:48] Marco: Redwood Optimize has some safety and moderation hooks; you can run post-processing filters and we integrate with common policy engines.

[20:20] Tara: operational runbooks — can we co-author runbooks for the integrated offering?
[20:26] Priya: totally, we provide runbook templates for partners and can co-author those for your managed offering.

[21:05] Speaker 3 (background): okay

[21:40] Marco: one more technical ask — please include peak concurrency and cold-start tolerance in the trace. if some customers need sub-100ms p50 that's a different sizing curve.

[22:10] Jamal: noted.

[23:00] Priya: let's recap next steps — I'll send partner deck, Marco will run sizing with traces, VectorCloud shares trace and legal templates, and we'll schedule the SE deep dive.

[23:20] Elena: yes, and let's target the week of Jan 11 for the deep dive.

[23:30] Priya: perfect. anything else from anyone?
[23:34] Tara: maybe just confirm who will own the dev work on your side for the terraform connector?
[23:40] Marco: Marco will be point for the terraform/API examples; Priya will coordinate docs.

[24:05] Jamal: thanks everyone, excited to move fast.
[24:12] Priya: thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and links.

[24:30] (last 28 minutes were Q&A and whiteboarding — transcript sampling continues with occasional crosstalk and partial sentences)

[25:15] Tara: so if we run a pilot with one customer, how do we estimate unit economics? can you provide cost-per-token estimates at 95th percentile?
[25:27] Marco: yes, we'll provide cost-per-1M tokens for your trace at different instance classes and show latency curves.

[26:00] Elena: note — our legal team will require a SOC 2 + data residency addendum, we might need a custom SLA for a few enterprise customers.

[26:18] Priya: that's fine — we often do addenda for enterprise pilots.

[27:00] Jamal: competitor question — MegaCloud AI offers a marketplace workflow, how is Redwood's partner experience different?
[27:08] Priya: Redwood aims at production-grade inference with strong observability, predictable unit economics, and flexible deployment modes — our differentiator is the runtime + ops tooling.

[27:40] Tara: small nit — do you provide example IaC for automated onboarding?
[27:46] Marco: yes, we have terraform examples and partner templates.

[28:10] Speaker 2 (background): mm-hmm

[28:50] Priya: ok I'll send a consolidated email after this with links: partner deck, security pack, partner onboarding template, and the perf sizing spreadsheet.

[29:20] Jamal: cool. any questions on our side?

[29:35] Elena: none from me.

[30:00] Priya: thanks again, we'll be in touch and set up that SE deep dive.

[30:10] (call wraps, some people stay to troubleshoot calendar invites)

Notes about transcript quality: auto-transcription had occasional mis-hears: "KV cache" appears as "kay vee cash" in one segment, Redwood product names occasionally truncated (e.g., "Redwood Dedicate"), and some speaker labels were generic; cleaned minimally for clarity.
